subject: Package-path workshop: seat vs throughput scenarios & action items
messages:
From: Emma Lin <emma@pulsehealth.io>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Packaging discussion — workshop prep

Thanks Jordan — quick summary of what we want to cover on the call: 

- Expected monthly token throughput: 150M tokens (burst to 300M).
- Primary latency target for patient-facing features: 350ms p95.
- We need HIPAA-aligned data routing (VPC/backhaul) and audit logs for 12 months.
- Prefer a mix of cheaper quantized variants for batch tasks, higher-quality for live chat.

Are you able to sketch two clean buying paths we can evaluate: (A) seat-oriented (fixed seat pools + feature add-ons) vs (B) throughput-oriented (committed tokens with feature entitlements)? Also want clear rollback/upgrade mechanics and any associated credits.

Attached is our traffic sample and a simple cost target (pulse_traffic_nov.csv). Can you confirm the right Redwood contacts for procurement/security on your side?

—Emma
Senior PM, PulseHealth

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Lin <emma@pulsehealth.io>, Raj Singh <raj.singh@pulsehealth.io>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Packaging discussion — workshop prep

Thanks Emma — this is perfect context.

Quick answers up front: procurement/security leads on our side are Ben Carter (sales lead, contracting/pricing) and Lauren Bishop (CS/ops for rollout + retention/credits). I’m copying both.

I’ll come prepared with:
- Two end-to-end scenarios (Seat-first and Throughput-first) with a clear migration path between them.
- Sample SLAs and what triggers a step-down/step-up.
- A proposed 90-day canary + grace/proration policy we typically use.

Action items before the call:
1) Emma: can you confirm whether the 12-month audit-log retention is a hard requirement or a preferred target?
2) Raj: if you have an internal headcount estimate for support triage, share that so we can size our onboarding credits.
3) Ben & Lauren: I asked for a short pricing workbook and a draft runbook — I’ll attach the first pass after the call.

Proposed time: today 3:00pm PT. If that works I’ll send a calendar invite.

—Jordan
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: Raj Singh <raj.singh@pulsehealth.io>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Emma Lin <emma@pulsehealth.io>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 11:09:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Packaging discussion — workshop prep

Jordan — 3pm PT works for us. To Emma's point: 12-month audit-log retention is a compliance requirement for now. We also expect to keep dev/test subsets for 90 days.

A couple of clarifiers for your scenarios: 
- If we pick seat-oriented, we need to understand how burst throughput is priced beyond the seat pool. Is it metered or credit-exchange?
- For throughput-first: what guardrails exist to keep latency within our 350ms p95 SLA under load? Any recommended model variants or routing policies?

We’re trying to keep the procurement as simple as possible; clear canary metrics and rollback steps will be the deciding factor.

—Raj
VP Engineering, PulseHealth

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 17:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: proposed packaging + discount posture (notes)

(Internal — do not forward)

Recap of the call and next internal asks after workshop:

- We should present three discrete options to PulseHealth during the workshop:
  1) Compact-seat bundle: fixed seat pools (up to 50 concurrency), per-seat entitlements for high-quality models, + metered overflow (per-token) for batch jobs.
  2) Commit-throughput bundle: committed monthly token volume with tiered unit pricing, feature toggles included; automatic step-up discounts after sustained usage.
  3) Hybrid flex: a small committed token baseline + seat pools for low-latency endpoints; includes 30% discount on quantized model units and a 60-day grace/proration.

- Discount posture: we can offer a headline 18% discount on a 12-month commit for option (2) if they commit to 9 months minimum and agree to a 60-day canary with our standard rollback triggers. If they prefer option (1) we can provide a one-time onboarding credit equal to two weeks of expected throughput (calculated from their traffic sample).

- Attachments to finalize before workshop: pricing-scenarios.csv (SKU examples), tier-matrix.pdf (feature entitlements table), pack_runbook_v1.xlsx (deployment canary runbook).

Next steps for Ben: please finalize the nominal pricing rows and prepare a short slide with what triggers a step-down (e.g., sustained 30% drop vs baseline for 14 days).

Lauren
Head of Customer Ops, Redwood Inference
